learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will master the rules of tense consistency and learn to transform sentences (Simple, Compound, Complex; Affirmative to Negative) without altering their core meaning.]
warm_up_hook: 🪄 Welcome to grammar magic! Imagine taking a sentence, completely changing its structure and words, yet keeping its meaning exactly the same. That's the power of Sentence Transformation! ✨

lesson_modules.teaching_content: A sentence must logically maintain its timeline. The fundamental rule: If the principal clause is in the past tense, the subordinate clause must also be in the past tense (exceptions for universal truths).
examples_or_templates: Incorrect: He said that he is coming.
Correct: He said that he was coming.
Universal Truth Exception: The teacher explained that the Earth revolves around the sun.

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Simple sentences have one independent clause. Compound sentences join two independent clauses using FANBOYS (For, And, Nor, But, Or, Yet, So). Complex sentences have one independent and one dependent clause joined by subordinating conjunctions (Although, Because, Since, If).
examples_or_templates: Simple: Seeing the bear, he ran away.
Compound: He saw the bear, so he ran away.
Complex: When he saw the bear, he ran away.

lesson_modules.teaching_content: You will often be asked to change an Affirmative sentence to Negative, use 'No sooner... than', or remove 'too... to' without changing the meaning.
examples_or_templates: Affirmative to Negative: 'He is always on time.' -> 'He is never late.'
Removing 'too': 'He is too weak to walk.' -> 'He is so weak that he cannot walk.'
No sooner: 'As soon as he arrived, it rained.' -> 'No sooner did he arrive than it rained.'

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Transform to a negative sentence without changing the meaning: 'Every cloud has a silver lining.'
options: No cloud has a silver lining.
There is no cloud without a silver lining.
Clouds do not have silver linings.
Not every cloud has a silver lining.
practice_mcq_quiz.correct_answer: There is no cloud without a silver lining.

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Choose the correct complex transformation of this simple sentence: 'In spite of working hard, she failed.'
options: She worked hard but she failed.
Although she worked hard, she failed.
She failed because she worked hard.
practice_mcq_quiz.correct_answer: Although she worked hard, she failed.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Rewrite the sentence using 'No sooner... than': 'As soon as the bell rang, the students rushed out.'
subjective_practice.hint: Start with 'No sooner did the bell...' and remember to use 'than' in the middle.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Transform this Compound sentence into a Simple sentence: 'You must work hard, or you will not pass.'
subjective_practice.hint: Use an infinitive phrase starting with 'You must work hard to...'

activity_or_assignment.title: 🔀 The Shape-Shifter Challenge
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Take the simple sentence: 'Being tired, the traveler sat under a tree.' Write it down. Now, transform it into a Compound sentence. Then, transform it into a Complex sentence. See how many ways you can say the exact same thing!

chapter_summary: ⭐ Maintain tense consistency: A past tense main clause usually forces past tense in the subordinate clause.
⭐ Simple = 1 clause. Compound = FANBOYS. Complex = Subordinating conjunctions (Although, Because).
⭐ Use opposites and negative structures ('not without', 'never') to transform affirmative sentences to negative ones seamlessly.
